title: Step Back From the Animal and the Photograph Gets Better
excerpt: Wildlife photography rewards closeness, but the strongest wildlife frames often do the opposite: they leave room for the place the animal lives in, and let the habitat do part of the storytelling.

title: A Shiny Surface Photographs What It Sees, Not What It Is
excerpt: A glossy bottle kept reflecting the props around it, and white paper only changed the reflection. The fix was a silver card that returned the bottle's own light to the camera, a lesson in thinking about reflections before reaching for a fix.

title: Your Camera Maker Has Not Abandoned Photography for Video
excerpt: Every new camera seems to add video features, and it is easy to read that as a rejection of stills photographers. DPReview's Richard Butler argues the opposite: video is catching up, photography was already mature, and the stills cameras are still coming.
